context.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud within sub-50ms latency while supporting secure case management and 7-year tamper-evident audits. It operates on AWS within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget, maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance for a three-engineer team.

## Key Elements
* Payment Gateway / Core Processing Engine
* Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System (AWS-hosted)
* Fraud Analyst, ML Engineer / Data Scientist, and Finance / Operations Manager
* Card Schemes / Identity Providers
* Archival Storage / Compliance Ledger

## Relationships
* Payment Gateway to Screening System: Synchronous gRPC over mTLS
* Fraud Analysts, ML Engineers, Finance Managers to Screening System: HTTPS via OIDC/OAuth2 with RBAC/MFA
* Screening System to Archival Storage / Compliance Ledger: Asynchronous, cryptographically signed event streams (AWS Kinesis to S3 Object Lock)

## Technology Stack
* AWS (eu-west-1): Managed cloud infrastructure fitting the €25k monthly budget and supporting a 3-engineer team
* gRPC over mTLS: Low-latency, secure machine-to-machine communication for sub-50ms P99 scoring
* OIDC/OAuth2: Standardized identity federation and access control for internal users
* AWS Kinesis and S3 Object Lock: Scalable event streaming and write-once-read-many storage ensuring 7-year tamper-evident auditability

## Rationale
Managed AWS services minimize operational overhead, enabling a three-engineer team to maintain the platform within strict budget limits. Decoupled synchronous scoring and asynchronous auditing satisfy high-throughput performance demands while strictly enforcing PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year non-repudiation.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform that evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations and manages suspicious payment reviews for a mid-size payment processor. It operates on AWS in the eu-west-1 region to ensure strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, high availability, and auditability.

## Key Elements
* Fraud Analyst, ML Engineer / Data Scientist, Finance / Operations Manager, Merchant / Merchant Success Manager, and Compliance / Risk Officer
* Payment Gateway / Core Processing Engine and Card Schemes / Identity Providers
* AWS API Gateway / NLB (Ingress)
* Fraud Scoring Engine (Go microservice)
* Case Management Backend (Java / Spring Boot with React UI)
* Audit Logger (AWS Lambda / Worker)
* Feature Store (AWS ElastiCache for Redis)
* Relational Store (Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL)
* Tamper-Evident Storage (Amazon S3 with Object Lock in Compliance Mode)
* Message Queue (Amazon SQS with AWS KMS encryption)

## Relationships
* Payment Gateway / Core Processing Engine routes authorization traffic to AWS API Gateway / NLB via HTTPS
* AWS API Gateway / NLB invokes Fraud Scoring Engine via gRPC
* Fraud Scoring Engine queries AWS ElastiCache for Redis via low-latency TCP
* Fraud Scoring Engine asynchronously publishes decision payloads to Amazon SQS
* Audit Logger consumes from Amazon SQS and writes tamper-evident logs to Amazon S3 with Object Lock
* Fraud Analysts and Managers access Analyst UI / Case Management via HTTPS/REST
* Case Management Backend persists state in Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL

## Technology Stack
* AWS API Gateway / NLB: Edge ingress and tokenization for PCI-DSS scope reduction
* Go: High-performance language for Fraud Scoring Engine to meet <50ms P99 latency
* Java / Spring Boot & React: Robust backend and frontend for Case Management and merchant analytics
* AWS ElastiCache for Redis: Low-latency feature store for real-time model scoring
* Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL: Relational persistence for case management data
* Amazon SQS: Asynchronous message decoupling to protect scoring latency
* Amazon S3 with Object Lock: WORM storage guaranteeing 7-year tamper-evident auditability

## Rationale
The architecture utilizes Go and gRPC to strictly satisfy the sub-50ms P99 performance requirement under heavy load. Asynchronous SQS queuing and S3 Object Lock compliance mode securely enforce 7-year tamper-evident auditability and PCI-DSS compliance without impacting real-time transaction latency or exceeding the 25,000 EUR monthly infrastructure budget.

AWS API Gateway / NLB.analysis:
## Overview
The system provides real-time payment fraud screening for card-not-present authorizations to protect transactions while ensuring sub-50ms latency. It handles case management, secure tokenization, and auditable decision-making under strict PCI-DSS Level 1 constraints.

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway / Core Processing Engine
- AWS Network Load Balancer (NLB)
- AWS API Gateway (HTTP API)
- AWS WAF
- Fraud Scoring Engine (Go)
- Case Management Backend (Java / Spring Boot with React UI)
- Audit Logger (AWS Lambda / Worker)
- Feature Store (AWS ElastiCache for Redis)
- Relational Store (Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL)
- Tamper-Evident Storage (Amazon S3 with Object Lock in Compliance Mode)
- Message Queue (Amazon SQS with AWS KMS encryption)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway / Core Processing Engine -> AWS Network Load Balancer: Forwards raw traffic [TCP/TLS]
- AWS Network Load Balancer -> AWS API Gateway: Forwards decapsulated requests [HTTP]
- AWS API Gateway -> Fraud Scoring Engine: Invokes real-time scoring [gRPC via VPC Link with mTLS]
- Fraud Scoring Engine -> Feature Store: Retrieves scoring features [RESP/TCP]
- Fraud Scoring Engine -> Message Queue: Publishes audit payloads [AWS SDK / SQS]
- Audit Logger -> Tamper-Evident Storage: Stores immutable compliance logs [HTTPS / S3 API]

## Technology Stack
- AWS (eu-west-1): Target cloud infrastructure within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget constraint.
- Go: Powers the Fraud Scoring Engine for high-throughput, low-latency processing.
- Java / Spring Boot & React: Powers the Case Management Backend and Analyst UI.
- Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL: Relational storage for structured transactional and case data.
- Amazon S3 with Object Lock: Tamper-evident storage satisfying the 7-year auditability requirement.

## Rationale
This architecture uses Go and gRPC to guarantee sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS. Edge tokenization via AWS services successfully minimizes the PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance boundary while remaining within the fixed budget.

Fraud Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
The Fraud Scoring Engine is a high-performance Go microservice that screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud within 50ms P99 latency while ensuring PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability. It evaluates transactions in real time, generates explainable risk scores, and gracefully handles outages to protect merchant revenue.

## Key Elements
- API Router & Fallback Handler (Go `net/http`)
- Feature Aggregator (Go concurrent routines)
- Scoring Evaluator with Feature Contribution Formatter (Go in-memory engine)
- Audit Publisher (Go SDK with HMAC-SHA256)
- External Systems: AWS API Gateway / NLB, AWS ElastiCache for Redis (Feature Store), Amazon SQS (Message Queue), AWS KMS

## Relationships
- AWS API Gateway / NLB -> API Router & Fallback Handler: Invokes scoring evaluation [mTLS / gRPC or HTTP/2]
- API Router & Fallback Handler -> Feature Aggregator: Concurrently fetches features [Go channels / In-memory function calls]
- Feature Aggregator -> AWS ElastiCache for Redis: Queries real-time features [Low-latency TCP / Redis Protocol]
- Scoring Evaluator -> Audit Publisher: Dispatches decision metadata and risk drivers [Buffered Go channel]
- Audit Publisher -> Amazon SQS: Publishes signed decision payloads [AWS SDK for Go over HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Go (Golang): Chosen for zero-garbage-collection predictability and ability to meet <50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS under a constrained memory footprint.
- AWS ElastiCache for Redis: Provides low-latency TCP data access for real-time feature aggregation.
- Amazon SQS with AWS KMS: Secures and buffers asynchronous audit logs with envelope encryption and tamper-evident signing.
- mTLS & TLS 1.3: Enforces strict transport security across all internal and external container boundaries.

## Rationale
This architecture uses Go's concurrency model and in-memory evaluation to meet stringent performance requirements without exceeding the 25,000 EUR monthly infrastructure budget. Layered security controls, tokenization boundaries, and explicit memory sanitization achieve PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and tamper-evident 7-year auditability.

Case Management Backend.analysis:
## Overview
The Case Management Backend is a Java Spring Boot container providing secure case review, bulk operations, and metric dashboards for fraud analysts. It ensures compliance, auditability, and efficient handling of suspicious transactions under strict AWS budget constraints.

## Key Elements
- Case Query Controller (Java/Spring MVC)
- Case Domain Service (Java/Spring)
- Bulk Action Processor (Spring Batch / SQS Consumer)
- Data Access Repository (Spring Data JPA)
- Metrics Aggregator (Spring Boot / Redis cache)
- React UI (Frontend accessed via AWS Cognito OAuth2/OIDC)

## Relationships
- React UI -> Case Query Controller: Accesses API and dashboards [HTTPS/REST]
- Case Query Controller -> Case Domain Service: Invokes business logic [Java Method Calls]
- Case Domain Service -> Relational Store (Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL): Reads/writes case states [PostgreSQL/JDBC, TLS 1.3]
- Bulk Action Processor -> Message Queue (Amazon SQS): Consumes bulk jobs [AWS SDK/SQS]
- Case Domain Service -> Tamper-Evident Storage (Amazon S3): Forwards immutable audit logs [AWS SDK/HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- Java 17 / Spring Boot: Robust backend framework for enterprise business logic and security integration
- Spring Batch / SQS: Asynchronous processing for high-volume bulk case resolution without HTTP timeouts
- Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL: Relational storage for case state persistence with column-level encryption via AWS KMS
- AWS ElastiCache for Redis: In-memory caching for low-latency metric aggregation (AHT, backlogs)
- AWS Cognito: Identity and access management enforcing OAuth2/OIDC and RBAC

## Rationale
This architecture scales effectively for a 3-engineer team by leveraging managed AWS services and familiar Spring patterns to meet sub-50ms constraints and strict 7-year audit rules. It maintains PCI-DSS compliance and stays within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

## Overview
[The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform that evaluates card-not-present transactions and provides case management for suspicious payments.]
[It ensures secure, auditable, and sub-50ms fraud decisions under strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance constraints.]

## Key Elements
* Personas: Fraud Analyst, Compliance Officer, External Regulators
* Containers: Audit Logger (AWS Lambda), Message Queue (Amazon SQS), Tamper-Evident Storage (Amazon S3)
* Audit Logger Components: Queue Consumer Component (Go), Canonical Formatter Component (Go), Storage Writer Component (Go)

## Relationships
* Queue Consumer -> Message Queue: Polls payloads [AWS SDK over HTTPS]
* Queue Consumer -> Canonical Formatter: Normalizes data [In-memory Go structs]
* Canonical Formatter -> Storage Writer: Passes formatted payload [In-memory function call]
* Storage Writer -> Tamper-Evident Storage: Writes audit logs with Object Lock [HTTPS / S3 API]
* Storage Writer -> AWS KMS: Signs payloads for cryptographic non-repudiation [AWS KMS API]

## Technology Stack
* AWS Lambda: Serverless execution for zero idle infrastructure cost within the 25k EUR budget
* Go: High-performance language for the AWS Lambda handler and internal components
* Amazon S3 Object Lock: Compliance Mode enforcement for tamper-evident 7-year audit retention
* AWS KMS: Cryptographic signing and encryption using customer-managed keys (CMK)
* Amazon SQS: Decoupled event ingestion secured via VPC Endpoint policies

## Rationale
[Serverless components minimize operational overhead for a 3-person engineering team while strictly adhering to the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.]
[Immutable storage and cryptographic signing satisfy PCI-DSS Level 1 mandates and 7-year auditability requirements.]

Feature Store.analysis:
## Overview
The Feature Store component provides low-latency real-time and historical feature data to power sub-millisecond payment fraud screening. It ensures high availability and strict PCI-DSS compliance while supporting real-time model updates.

## Key Elements
* Feature API Handler (Go)
* Feature Aggregator (Go)
* Feature Cache (Redis Core)
* Feature Backfill Worker (Go)
* AWS ElastiCache for Redis
* Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL
* Amazon SQS

## Relationships
* Fraud Scoring Engine -> Feature API Handler: Fetches real-time features [gRPC / Low-latency TCP with mTLS]
* Feature Aggregator -> Feature Cache: Updates real-time features [Redis RESP over TLS]
* Feature API Handler -> Feature Cache: Reads feature values [Redis RESP over TLS]
* Feature Backfill Worker -> Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL: Queries baseline historical features [JDBC over TLS]
* Feature Backfill Worker -> Feature Cache: Seeds historical aggregates [Redis RESP over TLS]
* Feature Aggregator -> Amazon SQS: Consumes real-time payment events [AWS SDK over HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
* Go: High-performance concurrency for API handling, aggregation, and backfilling within strict latency budgets
* AWS ElastiCache for Redis: In-memory store providing sub-millisecond retrieval and AES-256 encryption at rest
* Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL: Durable relational storage for baseline historical features
* Amazon SQS: Message queue for processing real-time payment event streams
* gRPC & Redis RESP: Low-overhead binary protocols for internal component communication

## Rationale
This component architecture achieves P99 latency below 50ms using in-memory caching while maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance through rigorous data isolation and encryption. It operates reliably within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget and supports a three-engineer team via standard, maintainable Go worker patterns.

Relational Store.analysis:
## Overview
The system provides real-time payment fraud screening for card-not-present transactions and managed case reviews for fraud analysts. It ensures sub-50 ms decisions, strict compliance, and 7-year auditability on AWS.

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Fraud Analyst, ML Engineer / Data Scientist, Finance / Operations Manager
- **External Systems**: Payment Gateway / Core Processing Engine, Card Schemes / Identity Providers, Archival Storage / Compliance Ledger
- **Containers**: AWS API Gateway / NLB, Fraud Scoring Engine (Go), Case Management Backend (Java / Spring Boot with React UI), Audit Logger (AWS Lambda / Worker), Feature Store (AWS ElastiCache for Redis), Relational Store (Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL), Tamper-Evident Storage (Amazon S3), Message Queue (Amazon SQS)
- **Relational Store Components**: Case Repository Component, Audit Ledger Index Component, Database Migration Manager

## Relationships
- Case Management Backend -> Relational Store: Persists and retrieves case state [PostgreSQL wire protocol (TCP/IP) via TLS 1.3]
- Audit Logger -> Relational Store: Streams advanced audit logs [PostgreSQL wire protocol (TCP/IP) via TLS 1.3]
- Database Migration Manager -> Relational Store: Executes schema migrations [Flyway / TCP/IP]

## Technology Stack
- **Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL (`db.m6g.xlarge`)**: Managed relational persistence layer balancing multi-AZ high availability with cost constraints.
- **AWS KMS & AWS Secrets Manager**: AES-256 storage-level encryption, transparent column-level encryption, and automated 30-day credential rotation for security compliance.
- **PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS) & Advanced Auditing**: Enforces strict data segregation for analysts and tamper-evident logging for PCI-DSS.
- **Flyway**: Zero-downtime schema migrations supporting rule and model evolution.
- **AWS (eu-west-1)**: Target cloud provider complying with infrastructure budget and residency requirements.

## Rationale
This architecture meets PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year audit mandates while staying within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget through managed AWS services. It empowers a three-engineer team to maintain high availability, security, and sub-200 ms case query latencies under peak loads.

The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud below 50 ms P99 latency while enabling secure analyst case management. It guarantees 7-year tamper-evident auditability for every decision under PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.

- AWS API Gateway / NLB, AWS Lambda / Worker, Amazon S3 with Object Lock
- Fraud Scoring Engine (Go), Case Management Backend (Java / Spring Boot with React UI)
- Feature Store (Amazon ElastiCache for Redis), Relational Store (Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL)
- Tamper-Evident Storage (Amazon S3 with Object Lock in Compliance Mode)
- Message Queue (Amazon SQS with AWS KMS encryption), Amazon Athena

## Relationships
- `Audit Logger` -> `Tamper-Evident Storage`: Appends immutable decision logs [HTTPS / S3 API via VPC Endpoint]

- `Fraud Scoring Engine` -> `Feature Store`: Retrieves user features [Redis Protocol / TCP]
- `Fraud Scoring Engine` -> `Relational Store`: Persists scoring rules and metadata [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol / TCP]

## Technology Stack
- AWS (eu-west-1): Target cloud infrastructure within fixed 25,000 EUR/month budget.
- Go & Java/Spring Boot: High-performance backend containers meeting strict P99 latency.
- Amazon S3 (Object Lock Compliance Mode): WORM storage guaranteeing 7-year tamper-evident retention.
- Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive: Cost-effective long-term storage tier for budget compliance.
- Amazon Athena: Serverless SQL querying engine for audit log analysis.

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless and managed AWS services to minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team while satisfying strict PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year auditability mandates. Lifecycle tiering to Glacier ensures long-term compliance remains within the 25,000 EUR/month budget.

Message Queue.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations to detect fraud and manage reviews while ensuring strict compliance. It processes up to 3,000 requests per second with sub-50ms P99 latency while adhering to PCI-DSS Level 1 standards.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts, ML Engineers / Data Scientists, Finance / Operations Managers
- AWS API Gateway / Network Load Balancer
- Fraud Scoring Engine (Go)
- Case Management Backend (Java / Spring Boot with React UI)
- Audit Logger (AWS Lambda / Worker)
- Feature Store (Amazon ElastiCache for Redis)
- Relational Store (Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL)
- Tamper-Evident Storage (Amazon S3 with Object Lock in Compliance Mode)
- Message Queue (Amazon SQS with AWS KMS encryption, comprising `fraud-decisions-queue` and `fraud-decisions-dlq`)

## Relationships
- Fraud Scoring Engine -> Message Queue: Asynchronously publishes decision payloads via HTTPS [Amazon SQS API, TLS 1.3]
- Message Queue -> Audit Logger: Consumes decision payloads for immutable logging [Event-driven consumption]
- Payment Gateway -> AWS API Gateway: Ingests payment authorization requests [HTTPS]
- Case Management Backend -> Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL: Persists review cases and analyst actions [SQL/TLS]

## Technology Stack
- AWS (eu-west-1): Cloud provider hosting the serverless and containerized infrastructure within a fixed budget of 25,000 EUR/month.
- Go & Java / Spring Boot: High-performance backend runtime environments for low-latency scoring and robust case management.
- Amazon SQS & AWS KMS: Serverless decoupling layer with customer-managed key encryption at rest to maintain PCI compliance.
- Amazon S3 (Object Lock Compliance Mode): Tamper-evident immutable storage ensuring 7-year audit retention.

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless and managed AWS services to minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team while guaranteeing sub-50ms latency. Strict data minimization, IAM policies, and immutable storage ensure compliance with PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year audit constraints within the fixed infrastructure budget.
